name: YorTIB-200
description: This Zenodo repository contains the reproducibility materials for the study "The Sovereignty Gap in Yoruba NLP: Orthographic Preservation and Contextual Lexical-Semantic Disambiguation." The project introduces YorTIB-200, a 200-item contextual lexical-semantic benchmark designed to examine the relationship between orthographic representation and contextual semantic disambiguation in Yoruba NLP. The benchmark focuses on six orthographically marked Yoruba lexical forms—ọ̀run, àṣẹ, ìwà, ọkọ, ẹ̀dá, and ògùn—and includes 24 semantic interpretations distributed across contextualized Yoruba sentences. Each benchmark item contains a Yoruba sentence, a focus word, four candidate meanings, and a gold-standard semantic label. The repository provides the benchmark data together with prediction outputs and computational materials for reproducing the reported analyses. The evaluation compares two representation conditions: a baseline condition and a sovereignty-preserving condition designed to retain linguistically meaningful orthographic information. Across the 200 benchmark items, the baseline condition correctly classified 77/200 items (38.5%), whereas the sovereignty-preserving condition correctly classified 199/200 items (99.5%), representing an absolute difference of 61.0 percentage points. In the paired analysis, 122 items changed from incorrect to correct, while one item remained incorrectly classified under both conditions. The exact McNemar test yielded p = 3.76 × 10⁻³⁷.
